clue.text: Twenty four hours on island for personal assistant

parts.note: the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea
one day of the week, a span of twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: An assistant is given a day's stay on an island as a perk.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the day follows the island. Man Friday is Robinson Crusoe's servant, hence a general helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A man Friday is a loyal male helper or factotum, named after Crusoe's companion.

clue.text: Plus points possessed by customer, it seems

indicators.note: what is possessed by a phrase sits inside it, so the letters are held within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of customer, all of it, and the start of seems

explanation.surface: A shopper appears to own some advantages.
explanation.definitionFit: Merits are good qualities or advantages, the points in favour of something.

clue.text: Peer is not a Tory, not upper class!

parts.note: a simple negative

indicators.note: the second not tells us to strip out the letter for the following class description

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservative party, so a Tory is a blue
U is the standard abbreviation for upper class

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a lord is neither Conservative nor posh.
explanation.walkthrough: Take U out of BLUE to leave BLE. The surface joke is that a peer would usually be both Tory and upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble is a member of the aristocracy, as is a peer of the realm.

clue.text: Perennial protesters seemingly being rude to barmen

indicators.note: rude in the sense of rough or unpolished, so the letters come out in a crude new arrangement

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Habitual demonstrators come across as rude to the pub staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent-a-mob is a crowd of people ready to protest at any cause, as if hired for the purpose.

clue.text: Sleepy part of commuter land?

parts.note: surface reading: a quiet, drowsy corner of the suburbs
setter's reading: a place where commuters merely sleep, since they work elsewhere all day

explanation.walkthrough: Sleepy hints at the word for a room full of beds, used of suburbs where people only spend the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory town is a suburb or satellite settlement whose residents travel elsewhere to work.

clue.text: Yankee needs attention for some time

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: An American demands to be listened to for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a specific period, twelve months of duration.

clue.text: Article of note about hotel

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the note goes around the next piece

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
NATO phonetic alphabet code word for this letter

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a hotel stay.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article.

clue.text: Plaudit is attempted, endless, but restrained

indicators.note: with no end, so the final letter is dropped
something restrained is held in, so one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: tried, cut short
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise was tried, but held back, never quite finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' looks like a conjunction in the surface, yet it is taken literally as letters placed inside the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an expression of praise or admiration, like a plaudit.

clue.text: Employ rotten gag: entertaining, somewhat!

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, and somewhat says only part of the run is taken

parts.note: the end of rotten, gag, and the first letter of entertaining

explanation.surface: Hire a terrible joke, which is mildly amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts in rotten and spills over into the first letter of entertaining itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone is to hire or employ them.

clue.text: Steal from home a bird

parts.note: to rob is to steal
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A command to burgle a house, with a bird thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: A robin is a small red-breasted songbird.

clue.text: Studying English commercial, interrupting call

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so these pieces go inside the next one

parts.note: to ring is to telephone
E is the abbreviation for English
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A student is disturbed by an English advertisement during a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading a subject means studying it, especially at a British university.

clue.text: On the subject of tie, match fixed!

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective meaning concerned with a theme

indicators.note: a fixed match is rigged, its result arranged differently from fair play

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Speaking of a drawn game, it was rigged!
explanation.definitionFit: Thematic means relating to a theme, the subject in question.

clue.text: Dive endlessly: you'll get a breather!

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a lunge is a sudden dive forward

explanation.surface: Stop diving all the time and you'll have a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Breather looks like a rest, but here it is the organ that does the breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lung is the organ of breathing, a playful sense of breather.

clue.text: Crazy vetoing I indulge

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits to being mad when blocking things while also pampering themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in to a wish is to yield, to indulge it.

clue.text: Line of children, one appearing to be in tears?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: schoolchildren walking in pairs in a long file

definitions.text: one appearing to be in tears?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the reptile said to weep false tears

explanation.walkthrough: Crocodile tears are a show of false grief, from the legend that the animal weeps as it eats its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a two-by-two file of pupils is called a crocodile, and the reptile gives fake tears their name.

clue.text: Informal eatery across road, one in British city

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the eatery goes around what follows

parts.note: caff is British slang for a cheap café
RD is the abbreviation for road
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cheap café over the road from where someone stands in a British city.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiff is the capital city of Wales, part of Britain.

clue.text: Our rap somehow causes commotion

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be arranged in another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Our hip-hop track stirs up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud public disturbance or outcry, a commotion.

clue.text: One tending to be less fat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who leans or inclines, tending in a direction
second meaning: comparative of an adjective for slim

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single phrase about getting slimmer; it splits after tending.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inclines is one who leans, and meat or a person with less fat is thinner.

clue.text: Stop and leave, quietly joining old ship

parts.note: p for piano, the musical direction to play quietly
Noah's Ark, the ancient vessel

explanation.surface: Instructions to halt and quietly board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To park a car is to stop and leave it somewhere.

clue.text: Print design showing kind countenance

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
countenance means the face

explanation.surface: A printed pattern depicts a friendly face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' reads as an adjective meaning friendly, but it is a noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface is a particular design of printed lettering, a font.

clue.text: Keep playing part in west London area

parts.note: to act is to play a part
on as in keep on, continuing

explanation.surface: Carry on acting a role in a district of west London.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together, act on suggests continuing a performance, as in to keep acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a district in the London Borough of Ealing, in the west of the capital.

clue.text: Turn fifty, pursuing a purpose

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Reaching your fiftieth birthday while chasing an aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursuing' places the fifty after the a. 'Turn fifty' reads as having a birthday, but turn is a go.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim or purpose one strives towards.

clue.text: Faraway river, alternatively island, with no company

parts.note: or offers an alternative
I is the abbreviation for island
taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A remote river, or else an island with no business on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a major river in Venezuela, distant from Britain.

clue.text: Unacceptable, going back and forth

indicators.note: the answer reads the same in either direction, which is what this phrase describes

parts.note: a phrase meaning not allowed, which reads identically both ways

explanation.surface: Wavering and dithering is not acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not on is British informal speech for it being unacceptable.

clue.text: One's concerned with fouls, primarily?

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of fouls

explanation.surface: A person whose main job is dealing with foul play.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a referee, while concerned with plus the head of fouls builds the short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A ref, short for referee, is the official whose job includes penalising fouls.

clue.text: Squire having depressing experience on network

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
a downer is something that makes you feel low

explanation.surface: A country gentleman has a miserable time on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the depressing experience after the network.
explanation.definitionFit: A squire was the chief landowner of an English rural parish.
